title: 2D Chamfer with no picks on a modelled chamfer rides the chamfer's top edge: the cone cuts 0.7 mm into the part and verify passes it

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

A 2D Chamfer with no picked edges, on a model whose edge already carries the modelled chamfer, puts the cone tip on the **top** edge of the chamfer (the top face's outline) and drops it by the width. The tip runs 1 mm inside the island wall. The posted G-code cuts a V into the part, and `verify` says `ok: true`, gouge 0. In the QA run `render_stock` painted the chamfer band as uncut rest, so the sim is not judging the cone that is posted (the edge-break credit appears to accept it as the intended break).

## Expected

Either the chamfer's lower edge (the wall at y = -15, z = 14) is the edge the cone rides, giving tip (y -15, z 14) and the modelled 1 x 1 chamfer, or the op refuses / says the edge is already chamfered. In any case verify must convict a cone that cuts below the model.

## Repro (MCP, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

**Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot.

1. `add_tool {catalog: "CM-1000-90"}` (90 deg taper, D10)
2. `add_operation {kind: "2D Chamfer", tool: "CM-1000-90", source: "flange", params: {width: 1}}` - no picks
3. `generate`, `verify`, `post {post: "Tormach PathPilot"}`

## Evidence (upstream main abe24ff09, same as v0.23.0)

```
G0 X75 Y15.999 Z25
G1 X75 Y15.999 Z-3 F300
G1 X25.05 Y15.999 Z-3 F1200
```
WCS Y15.999 / Z-3 is world y = -14.001, z = 14. The island wall is at y = -15; the chamfer surface runs from (y -15, z 14) to (y -14, z 15). A 90 deg cone with its tip at (-14, 14) reaches 0.71 mm normal into the chamfer face (it cuts a ~2 x 2 chamfer with a V below the modelled one). With `width: 0.5` the XY stays at Y15.999 and only Z changes (Z-2.5), so the width never moves the ride off the top edge.

`verify` on the same program: `ok: true`, findings `[]`, gate ok.

Workaround seen by the QA run: pick the chamfer's lower edge chain (z = 14) with `set_operation_geometry`; that posts `Y15 Z-3`, which is correct, and the sim is clean. `set_operation_area {offset: 1}` is refused ("a 2D Chamfer's cone lies on the picked wall - its ride cannot be offset or clipped").

Priority P1: posted G-code that cuts into the part and passes verify (Prime Directive). Related: #303, #529, #1891 (edge-break records and their credit).

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** the no-pick 2D Chamfer on a model with a modelled chamfer either rides the chamfer's lower edge (tip at the wall) or refuses by name; and a chamfer cone that cuts below the model is a blocking verify finding, not edge-break credit. Pinned by a test on this geometry (tip XY/Z asserted, verify verdict asserted).
